newsitem.title: USA: California withdraws reward in Cosby murder case.
newsitem.headline: California withdraws reward in Cosby murder case.

text.p: Honouring a request by entertainer Bill Cosby, California Gov. Pete Wilson withdrew Friday a $50,000 reward the state offered to help catch his son's killer.

Cosby asked state officials in late January to retract the reward, which was offered for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the murderer of Ennis Cosby, who was gunned down while changing a tire on a Los Angeles freeway.
Bill Cosby said he was grateful for the gesture but did not want taxpayer funds used for the reward.

Wilson rescinded the rewarding an executive order, saying he regretted that "the Cosby family has had to suffer additional pain in their time of grief and mourning by having to respond to a barrage of media attention with regard to rewards offered by the state and other entities."
"It is my hope that withdrawing this reward brings a close to this issue and takes a burden off of the Cosby family," Wilson said in a statement.
California Lt. Gov. Gray Davis, a Democrat, offered the $50,000 reward last month. He was acting governor while Wilson, a Republican, was in Asia. Wilson and Davis are political rivals.
Earlier this week, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors voted to rescind the $12,500 reward it had offered to help catch Ennis Cosby's killer. No arrests have been made in the case.
